target_customer: Data teams and business users at companies that need to find, document and govern their analytics data
problem: Most companies hold large amounts of undocumented, hard to find data, so people waste hours digging for the right table or metric and data teams repeat answers.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for a data catalog, lineage, observability and governance platform
product_category: Data catalog, data governance, AI analytics knowledge layer

founders.name: Etai Mizrahi
founders.background_notes: Background not found in sources used.

founders.name: Andrew McEwen
founders.background_notes: Listed as the only founder on the YC page; press and directories list him as co-founder and CTO.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed connectors to many warehouses and BI tools, metadata crawling, lineage parsing and search. Standard but broad engineering, with AI features added later.

defensibility.rationale: Many catalog vendors and open source tools existed, and integrations are copyable, so defensibility came mainly from documentation and metadata accumulating inside the product.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established catalog vendors and open source projects kept competing, and Atlassian bought Secoda in December 2025 to add a data catalog for its Rovo AI product.

market_need_then: Modern data stacks were spreading in 2021 and teams complained about finding and trusting data. No dated spend or complaint figures were collected.

branding.name_origin: One summary of a BetaKit interview says the CEO described the name as shorthand for making hard to find company data searchable; this was not seen in the primary article.

identity.visual_style: Product-focused marketing site with analyst award badges and customer ratings
identity.voice_and_tone: Positions as a trusted metadata foundation for AI analytics, emphasizing context and self-service

brand_strength.rationale: Known within the data tooling community and cited by data leaders as investors, but no sources show merch, mascot or press about the brand itself.

pivots.to: AI powered data management platform with governance, lineage and monitoring
pivots.why: Press describes the 2023 Series A as funding an AI powered modern data management platform including a monitoring product.

outcome_analysis: Secoda started as a Google-like search tool for company data, raised a seed led by Craft Ventures in late 2021 and a $14 million Series A in 2023, and broadened into a catalog, lineage and monitoring platform with AI features. It reached about 45 staff and in December 2025 Atlassian acquired it, with undisclosed terms, to give Rovo a data catalog.
notes: Seed amount was reported as 2.75 million Canadian dollars, so amount_usd is left null rather than converted; one outlet said about 2 million total before the Series A. Seed date shown as 2021-12 from the BetaKit headline period and a seed listing; the article said it closed at the end of October, so timing is approximate. Series A was announced in September 2023 but closed in June per BetaKit. Competitor search returned only 2023 and later vendor comparison pages, so none are listed as dated near founding. Revenue figure of 1.9 million in 2024 appears only on one aggregator and is not used.
